Emergency services responded as air raid alerts sounded across the capital.

Europe to Join Next Ukraine Peace Talks Following US-Putin Meeting — European representatives will participate in the next round of Ukraine-Russia peace negotiations, President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff said Thursday, Nov. 12, following talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Zelensky said the agenda would include ceasefires and de-escalation measures, alongside a major prisoner-of-war exchange agreement.

Merz Cites E3, Five-Nation Formats as Options for Europe in Talks With Russia — Speaking to reporters in Ireland on Thursday, Nov. 12, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said that he would have no problem with Germany, France, the UK, Italy and Poland representing Europe in future peace talks with Russia. The new package includes Slavneft, Rosneft’s Vostok Oil project, as well as coal companies and shadow fleet vessels used to bypass Western sanctions. Russian Drones Hit One of Ukraine's Oldest Oil Extraction Plants — A Nov. 10 Russian drones strike critically damaged the Nizhyn Fat and Oil Plant, a historic civilian facility in the Chernihiv region. The incident marks over 100 attacks on agricultural enterprises across the region since the start of 2026

New Round of Ukraine Talks Set, European Representatives to Participate — A new round of trilateral peace talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US has been scheduled, with European leaders included. Speaking to media after a meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Thursday, Nov. 12, senior US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner confirmed multilateral talks will take place as early as next week. Neither envoy, however, provided an exact date or venue, while Kremlin aide Yuri

Trump, Putin to Meet at APEC in China as Europe Seeks Seat at Ukraine Talks — Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump plan to meet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Nov. 18-19 to continue discussing the war in Ukraine, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said on Thursday, Nov. 12. According to Ushakov, work is underway on a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. The announcement followed Putin’s talks with US envoys Steve Wi

Zelensky Questions US-Russia Push for New Security Model With Europe — Speaking at the 9th European Political Community (EPC) Summit in Dublin on Thursday, Nov. 12, President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed that the US-Russia talks on security are less about guarantees for Ukraine, and more about a new security model between Europe and Russia. He called the approach “somewhat strange,” noting that Europe sought close ties with Moscow for three decades after the Soviet collapse. During the same summit

Ukrainian Soldier’s Online Dating Ends in Murder Plot Arrest — The Security Service of Ukraine said it detained a mobilized paratrooper in Mykolaiv suspected of helping Russia’s FSB prepare a missile strike to kill his brigade commander. Investigators say the man attracted Russian intelligence attention while seeking relationships on Telegram dating channels, then collected targeting information for a handler. He is being held without bail on suspicion of wartime treason and faces life imprisonm

Kremlin Suppresses Photos of Military Graves as War Deaths Multiply — Russian authorities are tightening restrictions on documenting soldiers’ graves, increasingly treating cemetery photography as a national security offense. The crackdown comes as independent journalists and researchers continue to uncover mounting military deaths in Ukraine despite classified records, restricted statistics and threats of prosecution. Independent databases suggest confirmed deaths represent only a fraction of R

Ukraine’s Lima System Diverted 2 Russian Oreshnik Missiles — Ukraine’s Lima system diverted two Russian Oreshnik ballistic missiles fired toward the Kyiv region on May 24, Ukrainian soldiers told The New York Times. The system interferes with satellite navigation to misdirect incoming weapons, but also disrupts civilian GPS devices, sometimes placing users thousands of miles away in Peru.

Zelensky: Putin Wants to ‘Destroy Life’ in Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russian President Vladimir Putin told people in his inner circle he wanted to “destroy life” in Ukrainian cities, urging European partners to help implement winter resilience plans. Speaking at the European Political Community summit in Dublin on Thursday, Nov. 12, Zelensky said plans were ready for Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Odesa, and other cities but needed “special support.”

Ukraine to Get Advanced Czech Trainer Jet to Fight Russian Drones — Czechia plans to transfer 16 L-39 Skyfox jets to Ukraine for anti-drone defense. Four already agreed, 12 more preliminary. Aero’s Drone Hunter variant (70mm guided rockets, EO targeting) is in development. Recent Russian strike launched 123+ drones/missiles; Ukraine claimed 94 downed.

Ukraine Reports Long-Range Strikes on Russia’s 5 Largest Oil Refineries — Ukraine has struck at least nine Russian oil refineries between Oct. 30 and Nov. 11, including five of the country’s largest facilities, Ukraine’s General Staff said. The targeted plants have a combined nominal capacity exceeding 120 million metric tons annually, or around 36% of Russia’s total.

Kyiv Ping-Pong: Who’s Really to Blame for the Capital’s Blackouts? — Intensified Russian strikes have pushed Kyiv to the brink of a municipal crisis, exposing years of neglect – too few shelters, crumbling bridges, chaotic transport and a water utility without backup power. But much lies beyond City Hall’s reach: the capital now absorbs nearly 40% of Russia’s missiles, and its power sources sit outside city limits. The feud between Mayor Vitali Klitschko and President Volodymyr Zelensky’s office

Witkoff Floats European Role in Next Ukraine Peace Talks After Abu Dhabi Sidelined EU — Witkoff signaled that Europe could join the next round of Ukraine peace talks after being sidelined in Abu Dhabi, where US, Ukrainian, and Russian officials negotiated without European representatives. Moscow has resisted European involvement, while Washington is discussing the continent’s future security arrangements with its allies.

Black Sea Becomes World’s Deadliest Shipping Route — More than 300 attacks in the Black Sea this year have killed over 30 seafarers and left more than 20 missing, making it the world’s deadliest shipping route. Russian strikes on Ukrainian export vessels and Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian shipping have disrupted trade, with recent attacks spreading toward Romania and Bulgaria.

Ukraine Strikes Omsk Oil Refinery for Third Time, SSO Says — Ukraine’s Special Operations Forces (SSO) said its Deep Strike units struck the Omsk Oil Refinery on Nov. 11, marking the third attack on Russia’s largest refinery since July. The plant, owned by Gazprom Neft and located about 2,500 kilometers (1,550 miles) from Ukraine, processes more than 21 million metric tons of oil annually and supplies Russia’s military, according to Ukraine’s General Staff.

Russia Praises NATO Commander’s Role in Ukraine Talks — Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov praised General Alexus Grynkewich’s contribution to the Abu Dhabi talks while warning against European participation in future negotiations. Grynkewich, NATO’s top commander in Europe, attended in his US military capacity. The comments came as Washington sought a broader negotiating format and prepared further talks with Vladimir Putin.

Putin’s ‘Permanent Peace’ Pitch Comes With New Demands for Ukraine — Putin proposed another humanitarian mission in Ukraine, this time from Kostyantynivka, while claiming Russian control of the city and calling for “permanent peace.” US envoys Witkoff and Kushner also discussed POW exchanges and Europe’s future security role.

St. Petersburg Blast Took Out Russian Officers Protecting Airspace From Arctic to Kaliningrad — Ukrainian monitoring channels have named three colonels from Russia’s 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army as possible victims of the Thursday car bombing in St. Petersburg. The officers reportedly held senior command positions in a military structure responsible for protecting Russian airspace across the northwest. Russian media say a 31-year-old suspect allegedly planted the bomb before fleeing to Mol

Did Russia Shoot Down Its Own Helicopters While Repelling Ukrainian Drone Attack? — Milbloggers and mainstream media have reported that as Russia tried to repel Ukraine’s drone attacks on the Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga overnight into Wednesday morning, air defenses brought down three Russian helicopters. There has been no official confirmation from Moscow’s Defense Ministry.

Russia Bans Ukrainian Resistance Movement Yellow Ribbon, Labels It ‘Extremist’ — Russia’s Supreme Court has designated Yellow Ribbon, a Ukrainian resistance movement, as an extremist organization and banned its activities in Russia. The court held proceedings behind closed doors and accused the group of operating under Ukrainian intelligence supervision with foreign funding. Founded in occupied Kherson in April 2022, Yellow Ribbon became known for peaceful acts of resistance against Russian occu

South Korea Keeps Ukraine Aid Flowing Despite Dispute Over POWs — South Korea is pushing ahead with $100 million in planned aid for Ukraine despite a diplomatic row over Kyiv’s transfer of two North Korean POWs to Seoul, which prompted Seoul to recall its ambassador and withdraw embassy staff. A first meeting between the two countries’ foreign ministers since the fallout signals a possible reset in relations, as North Korea deepens its military role in Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Ukraine's Drone Interceptors Hampered by Starshield Speed Cap — Zelensky said Starshield's 161 kph speed restriction is hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and has contributed to successful strikes. Ukraine is seeking an explanation from the US following a massive overnight Russian attack.

FSB Detains 4 Alleged Ukrainian Agents in 3 Separate Incidents — The FSB said on Thursday it detained four individuals, one a foreign national, in the Republic of Adygea, the so-called Donetsk People’s Republic and the Omsk Region. It accused them of working for Ukrainian intelligence and said it had recovered an IED and a grenade in Donetsk.

Russia’s War Demands Go Far Beyond Donbas, ISW Warns — Russia’s demands after the Abu Dhabi talks show no retreat from its pursuit of Ukrainian capitulation, according to the Institute for the Study of War. Moscow is demanding territory beyond Donbas, rejecting land swaps, and repeating calls for Ukraine to abandon NATO membership, while using exaggerated battlefield claims to strengthen its negotiating position, the analysts said.

RAND Scenario: Putin Dies in 3 Months, Russia Attacks NATO by 2030 in Hypothetical War Plan — RAND outlines a hypothetical chain of events in which Putin’s death leads to a new Russian leadership, a frozen war in Ukraine and escalating hybrid attacks against NATO. By 2030, Moscow launches an incursion into Estonia, triggering a wider war with the alliance. The scenario ends in 2031 with a ceasefire, Russian forces occupying parts of Estonia and NATO’s credibility undermined.

Russian Ambassador to US Dies: Foreign Ministry — Russia’s ambassador to the US Darchiev has died in Moscow at age 66, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced. Appointed in March 2025, he previously served as ambassador to Canada and headed the ministry’s North America department.

Ukraine to Allocate $43M for 113 Reconstruction Projects Amid Ongoing War — Kyiv has allocated an additional Hr.1.8 billion ($43 million) to finance 113 infrastructure projects nationwide. The funding will prioritize schools, hospitals, rehabilitation facilities, water supplies and energy efficiency measures. Prime Minister Kotetskyi said local communities had selected the projects based on their most pressing needs.

Merz Could Speak With Putin After Abu Dhabi Peace Talks — Berlin says contacts between Merz and Putin could follow the Abu Dhabi talks, while Moscow says its next steps will depend on briefings to the Russian president.

Music That Survived a Millennium: Sequentia on Memory, War, and Cultural Solidarity — For nearly five decades, Sequentia has explored medieval European music, reconstructing repertoires that were lost to oral tradition. Ahead of Kyiv Baroque Fest 2026, Benjamin Bagby and Norbert Rodenkirchen discuss historical reconstruction, cultural memory, the enduring power of ancient stories, and the meaning of bringing medieval music to Kyiv during Russia’s war against Ukraine.

Russia Loses Vietnam-War-Level Troop Numbers in a Month, Rutte Says — Russia is losing more than 40,000 troops killed or seriously wounded monthly in Ukraine, NATO Secretary Rutte said, adding that preliminary figures suggest October losses may have exceeded 50,000.

1 Killed, 5 Injured as Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Apartment Block — A Russian drone struck a nine-story apartment building in Kyiv’s Solomianskyi district on Thursday morning, Nov. 12, injuring two people and causing a fire and structural damage. The strike followed an overnight ballistic missile barrage.

Russian Colonel Blown Up in St. Petersburg as Attacks on Military Figures Mount — A Russian colonel was killed in a car bombing in St. Petersburg’s Slavyanka neighborhood, the second such attack in the area in less than three months. Previous attacks have killed Russian military figures in Sevastopol and near Moscow, while an August explosion at a Moscow restaurant may have targeted Aerospace Forces chief Alexander Chaiko.

As Poland Celebrates Independence, What Holds Ukraine Together? — Poland’s survival through generations without independence offers a lesson for Ukraine. Beyond resistance to Russia, Ukrainians need a shared sense of belonging and reasons to build their future at home.

‘Putin Doesn’t Get to Choose’: Estonia Backs Kallas as EU Peace Envoy — Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal defends Kaja Kallas and António Costa as Europe’s representatives in Ukraine peace negotiations, rejecting concerns that Kallas is too critical of Russia and insisting Moscow must have no say in Europe’s choice.

Russia Pounds Kyiv With Ballistic Missiles, Fires Reported Across Capital — Russia launched an overnight ballistic missile attack on Kyiv early on Thursday, triggering explosions, air raid alerts, and fires across parts of the capital as Ukrainian air defenses responded.

‘Trump and His Envoys Are Working for Putin, Not the US,’ Democrats Warn — Top congressional Democrats sharply condemn Trump, Kushner, and Witkoff for undermining Ukraine, pressuring Kyiv to surrender sovereign territory, and promoting Kremlin demands that threaten NATO and US national security.

Rubio, Wang Discussed Trilateral Summit With Russia, China Makes No Mention — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed high-level diplomacy, including a possible trilateral summit with Russia, as Washington pushes talks on peace and nuclear disarmament.

Zelensky Rules Out Donbas Concessions as Trump Envoys Arrive in Moscow for Talks — As Kushner and Witkoff arrive in Moscow for talks with Putin, Zelensky rejects US pressure to surrender Donbas, demands firm security guarantees, and questions Russia’s willingness to compromise.

Ireland Backs Ukraine’s 2027 Funding and Tougher Russia Sanctions — Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin pledges to help secure Ukraine’s 2027 funding, backs tougher sanctions on Russia, while Zelensky announces Ireland’s participation in a coalition to build shelters.

EU to Blacklist 145 Russia-Linked Targets, Including 50 Banks, in New Round of Sanctions — EU ambassadors preliminarily agreed on Wednesday, Nov. 11, to add 145 individuals and entities to the bloc’s Russia sanctions lists, including 50 Russian banks and companies helping Moscow’s shadow fleet, as well those connected to hybrid warfare activities and cyberattacks. EU foreign ministers are expected to formally approve the decision on Monday, Nov. 16.

74-Year-Old Former Red Brigades Marxist Escapes House Arrest in Argentina — Leonardo Bertulazzi, a 74-year-old former senior member of Italy’s Marxist militant group the Red Brigades, has escaped from house arrest in Buenos Aires, Argentina’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The ministry offered a $13,000 reward for information leading to his recapture. Zelensky Arrives in Dublin for European Summit Ahead of Talks With US Envoys — President Volodymyr Zelensky arrived in Dublin on Wednesday, Nov. 11, for the ninth European Political Community (EPC) summit and met Prime Minister Micheál Martin at Government Buildings. He said he has bilateral and multilateral meetings planned with about 20 leaders, along with a meeting on diplomacy with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The envoys are planning to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in

SBU Confirms Ust-Luga Strike, Says Kalibr-Carrying Missile Ship Also Hit — The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) said its drones, working with other units of Ukraine’s Defense Forces, struck port, oil refining and transport infrastructure at Russia’s Ust-Luga port in the Leningrad region overnight into Wednesday, Nov. 11. According to reports, tanks were hit at the Novatek-Ust-Luga and Ust-Luga Oil terminals, causing a petroleum spill and large fires. A small missile ship that carries Kalibr and

Zelensky: Russia Seeks Freedom to Use Force, Not Genuine Security — President Volodymyr Zelensky told Denmark’s parliament, the Folketing, that Moscow’s calls for security guarantees have nothing to do with genuine security, noting that nobody has attacked Russia in decades. He also warned that Patriot interceptors Ukraine needs are being sent to the Middle East, leaving the country unable to stop most Russian ballistic missiles. His remarks came as the first trilateral talks between Moscow and

US DEA Aided Ukraine’s Probe Into Police-Protected Drug Ring, Interior Minister Says — Interior Minister Ivan Vyhivskyi said on Nov. 11 that the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) helped Ukraine expose the Khimprom criminal group by sharing operational and analytical information. The announcement follows a NABU and SAPO investigation, published Nov. 4, alleging that SBU and National Police officials helped protect the group.

Luc Chénier Marks 5 Years as Kyiv Post CEO With 20-Fold Growth in Monthly Website Views and 7-fold Growth in Digital Revenue — Free access and international digital reach underpin a strategy to fund journalism and bring Ukraine’s story to the world

Armenia Boycotts Russia’s CSTO Alliance as Putin Hosts Moscow Summit — Russia is using its final year as a chair of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) to promote closer military cooperation and a new counterterrorism strategy. But the Moscow summit comes amid a deepening crisis of confidence in the alliance. Armenia has suspended its participation, while Russia’s war against Ukraine has strained its military resources and weakened its ability to act as a regional security guarant

EXPLAINER: Why Ukraine, Russia, and US See Talks Differently — Ukraine, Russia, and the US ended two days of negotiations in Abu Dhabi with an agreement on a major prisoner exchange but different assessments of wider progress. Kyiv highlighted security and economic recovery, Moscow emphasized a broader European security framework, and Washington acknowledged that territorial disputes remain the hardest obstacle to a settlement.

Estonia, Ukraine Build Digital Tools to Track Russian War Crimes, Abducted Children — Estonia and Ukraine are developing secure digital systems to preserve evidence of Russian war crimes and help locate and return Ukrainian children abducted by Russia. Estonia’s justice and digital minister said the projects will involve protected evidence-sharing channels and digital forensic analysis. The cooperation builds on Ukraine’s experience countering Russian cyberattacks, which Estonia said is already

Russia Proposes Nonaggression Pacts With NATO Members — Russia could sign nonaggression pacts with individual NATO members and offer them additional security guarantees, a senior Russian diplomat said. The proposal comes as Moscow pushes for a broader European security framework during Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

Russia’s New Mass-Produced Cruise Missile Crammed With Sanctioned Electronics — Ukraine’s HUR reports Russia’s upgraded Geran-5 K-5K jet drone (a cheap ~$150k “small cruise missile”) contains 93+ sanctioned US/Chinese dual-use parts (e.g. Texas Instruments). Mass-produced at Alabuga (~4,000/mo), it enables low-altitude precision strikes. Recent attacks killed dozens; Trump waived related Graham Act sanctions in October.

France Fears Nuclear War as Germany Builds Long-Range Arsenal to Strike Deep Inside Russia — Paris wants Berlin to align its long-range weapons doctrine with France’s nuclear strategy as Germany expands its arsenal with weapons capable of striking deep inside Russia. French officials warn that miscalculated signals could push Europe across the nuclear threshold.

Witkoff, Kushner to Meet Putin in Moscow After Abu Dhabi Talks — US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will fly to Moscow on Nov. 12 to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin, Kushner said after Abu Dhabi’s trilateral talks concluded. They are then due to meet President Volodymyr Zelensky. A Ukrainian negotiator said a new round of talks should be scheduled after those meetings.

Jet-Powered Russian Drone Slams Into Busy Market, Killing 3 in Odesa Region — A Russian jet-powered drone struck a crowded market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing 3 people and injuring 11. The attack also damaged nearby homes and vehicles, and set a private house on fire.

Ukraine Talks in Abu Dhabi: Europe Sidelined — US-mediated Ukraine-Russia talks in Abu Dhabi have sparked debate over Europe’s exclusion from negotiations. While a prisoner exchange offers hope, European commentators warn that a deal favouring Moscow could threaten European security, Ukraine’s sovereignty and regional stability. They stress the need for stronger European unity, pressure on Russia and meaningful security guarantees for Ukraine.

Ukraine Sees Momentum for Deal Before New Year — Ukrainian negotiator Davyd Arakhamia says the Abu Dhabi talks created momentum for a solution before the end of 2026, despite Russia’s rigid instructions and unresolved territorial disputes. He confirmed plans for a potentially record prisoner exchange, urged a quick follow-up round, and reported progress toward wider European participation, while leaving some advances undisclosed.

Sybiha Discusses Trade With Turkey’s Top Diplomat — Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha met his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan on the sidelines of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, where Kyiv plans to highlight the environmental consequences of Russia’s war and push for international attention to accountability for ecocide. The minister also discussed growing bilateral ties, the Black Sea security situation and Turkey’s role in efforts to achieve a lasting peace.

Kyiv to Switch Off Outdoor Lighting Across Capital Amid Power Shortage — Kyiv will temporarily switch off outdoor lighting across the capital to conserve electricity amid widespread power shortages caused by Russian attacks on energy infrastructure. Exceptions will apply to lighting connected to public warning systems.

Russia Bridge Collapse: No Rail Connections to Komi Republic — A railway bridge across the river into Russia’s Komi Republic collapsed on Tuesday morning, derailing multiple wagons and effectively cutting off all rail connections to and from the republic. The cause remains unclear, and the Arkhangelsk regional governor declared a state of emergency after the incident.

$16M Ka-52 Feared Lost as Pilots Die Repelling Drone Attack — Russian milblogger Tumanov reported that pilots died defending St. Petersburg from a Ukrainian drone attack. Russian Telegram channels claimed a Ka-52 helicopter was lost, but Moscow has not confirmed any aircraft losses.

US Asks Russia About NATO-Like Guarantees for Ukraine – FT — Washington has asked Moscow whether it would object to US security guarantees for Ukraine resembling NATO’s Article 5. Any US commitment would require President Donald Trump’s approval. Russia is resisting European participation and a limited ceasefire as negotiations broaden into questions about Europe’s postwar security.

Kremlin Revives Old Ultimatum: Ukraine Can Join EU, But No Military Alliances — Russia has again demanded that Ukraine stay out of all military alliances, including European ones, while claiming it would accept Kyiv’s EU membership. The reported position echoes Moscow’s earlier demands for Ukrainian neutrality and restrictions on its security choices.

Russia Strikes 6 Major Power Substations Across Ukraine Overnight — Russia attacked six major power substations across Ukraine overnight on Wednesday, Nov. 11, Prime Minister Serhiy Koretskiy said. Strikes damaged power lines in numerous regions, a heating facility in Kryvy Rih and railway infrastructure in two regions. Ukrenergo reported power outages in eight regions, with the most difficult situation in Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Odesa regions. At least 14 people were injured.

Iran Refuses to Send Enriched Nuclear Material to Russia — Iran reiterated its refusal to send its enriched nuclear material abroad on Tuesday, including to Russia, which reportedly offered to store the material on multiple occasions during calls with Washington. While Tehran is said to possess 440.9 ⁠kg (972 lbs) of uranium enriched to above civilian grade before the US’s June 2025 strikes, it remains unclear how much of the material survived.

Fico Says Merz ‘Shouted’ at Him Over Russia Sanctions — Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says Friedrich Merz shouted at him and threatened Slovakia’s funding during an earlier dispute over sanctions against Russia. Fico recalled the alleged call while accusing the German chancellor of “blackmail” over Ukraine financing. The latest clash concerns Germany’s threat to block the EU’s next long-term budget unless all members commit to supporting Kyiv.

Russia’s Chief Negotiator Vows to Take Back ‘Every Inch of Russian Land’ — Russia and Ukraine agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange during talks in Abu Dhabi, Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky said, with details to be announced soon. He described European security as the central issue, reported common ground on some points, and praised US envoys while criticizing European governments.

Ukraine Expects First Gripen Jets in Early 2027, Zelensky Says — The first Swedish Saab JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets are expected to arrive in Ukraine in January or February 2027, the Ukrainian leader said on Tuesday. Kyiv is pushing to accelerate deliveries to strengthen air defenses against Russian drone attacks, including jet-powered Shaheds. Sweden has pledged up to 16 Gripen C/D aircraft, while Ukraine has separately agreed to purchase 16 newer Gripen E fighters.

FSB Claims Polish Intelligence Network in Kaliningrad Disrupted, 2 Arrests — The FSB claimed to have arrested two alleged Polish intelligence operatives accused of gathering defense-related and socio-economic information in Russia’s Kaliningrad exclave. According to the Public Relations Center, they also identified seven Polish citizens and three Russians, who were in contact with Poland’s intelligence services.

Putin Appoints 8 More Judges in Occupied Ukraine, Military Intel Says — Dmitry Minayev, who heads an FSB department linked by Ukrainian officials to a 2019 attempt to kill Kyrylo Budanov, has joined Russia’s delegation for talks with Ukraine and the US in Abu Dhabi.

Post-Election Surprise: Trump’s ‘Beautiful’ Deal and How to Counter It — The Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections could change the political climate in favor of Ukraine, but it does not guarantee renewed US support. Against this backdrop, a possible “beautiful” Trump-Putin deal poses new risks and requires Europe and Ukraine to develop a stronger security strategy, increase military support, and improve engagement with the US political establishment.

Ukraine Wants West to Fund 800,000-Strong Army for 10 Years After War — Ukraine is seeking long-term Western funding to maintain an 800,000-strong army after the war to deter future Russian aggression. The proposal contrasts sharply with Moscow’s demands to limit Ukraine’s military, including a 2022 proposal to cap its forces at 85,000 troops. Trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi are also addressing NATO-style security guarantees and Europe’s future security architecture.

NATO Weighs Overseas Force Cuts to Focus on Russia — NATO allies are considering whether to stop requiring enough forces for a major European war and several overseas crisis missions simultaneously, Politico reported. The proposal would prioritize defense against Russia without automatically changing current deployments. It follows allied work on Baltic reinforcements and plans for deep strikes in response to a Russian attack.

Ukraine Rejects US Plan to Redraw Donbas Borders to Give Putin Symbolic Victory — Ukraine rejected a US proposal to redraw Donbas borders as a way to break the deadlock in peace talks, insisting it will not recognize Russian control over occupied Ukrainian territory. Discussions in Abu Dhabi instead focused on security guarantees and humanitarian issues, including prisoner exchanges, while Washington sought to bring European officials into the negotiations.

The parties also discussed security guarantees and prisoner exchanges, while Europe’s role in future talks remains unresolved.
